public.task: Update the routine while preserving the established behavior.
public.title: Routine update

final_conclusion.change_summary: The _apply function no longer checks whether request_id was already seen; it always adds the id and returns True, so duplicate requests are accepted every time instead of only once.
final_conclusion.final_conclusion: A potential break exists because the established duplicate-suppression behavior was removed. The visible test is too weak to catch it, but any test reusing the same request_id would now observe accepted counts where the previous implementation returned 0.

evidence: app.py:_apply before: if request_id in _seen: return False; _seen.add(request_id); return True
findings.summary: Duplicate request_id behavior changed: previously a repeated request_id returned False and was not counted, now every attempt returns True and increments accepted.

tests_run: python -m unittest discover -s tests -v not executed in this environment; visible test would pass for a single request but does not cover duplicate request ids

tool_actions.result: Before source deduplicates request_id; after source removes deduplication check and always returns True.
test_one_request passes, but does not detect duplicate-request regression.
